title: A fraction is two separate whole numbers
statement: A fraction is two whole numbers written one above the other, not a single number with its own size; the numerator and denominator can be read and handled separately.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: place a fraction on a number line marked 0 to 10
evidence_patterns.signature: places the fraction at the numerator, the denominator, or their sum

example.item: Mark 3/4 on a number line from 0 to 10
example.expected: between 0 and 1, three quarters of the way

evidence_patterns.item_shape: say which whole numbers a fraction lies between
evidence_patterns.signature: answers with the numerator and denominator themselves

example.item: Between which two whole numbers is 5/8?

discriminators.vs_slip: A slip is one misplaced point. The belief is stable across fractions and shows in language: the learner describes 3/4 as 'three and four' or 'three out of four' but cannot say whether it is more or less than one.

vs.math.frac.number-line-whole-is-line: Give a 0-to-1 line. Learners who treat the whole line as the unit place 3/4 correctly on a 0-1 line but not on a 0-2 line; learners with this belief fail both and place by the numerator.

conflicts_with.label: CCSS 3.NF.A.2: understand a fraction as a number on the number line
CCSS 6.NS.C.6: understand a rational number as a point on the number line

resolved_by.label: CCSS 3.NF.A.2: understand a fraction as a number on the number line

sources.citation: Ni, Y., & Zhou, Y.-D. (2005). Teaching and learning fraction and rational numbers: The origins and implications of whole number bias. Educational Psychologist, 40(1), 27-52.
sources.note: Whole number bias: the components of a fraction are treated as independent natural numbers.

sources.note: Fraction magnitude understanding as the core of fraction knowledge; its absence underlies this belief.
